issues.passage: Budget cuts were meant to invigorate the program by eliminating training and travel support.
issues.why: Invigorate is used correctly for intended strengthening/energizing; a counterproductive method does not make the verb itself wrong usage.

fix.correctPassage: A change of leadership can invigorate an organization that has grown stagnant.
wrongPassages: The endless briefing seemed to invigorate staff, who left more exhausted than when they arrived.
The layoffs invigorated the department, leaving remaining staff depleted and demoralized.
Physicians warned that sleepless nights would invigorate patients recovering from surgery.
